stem.en: You look at a cell that is not dividing, and no rod-shaped chromosomes can be seen in its nucleus. Where is its DNA?

text.en: It has left the nucleus, and it comes back only when the cell gets ready to divide.

feedback.en: DNA stays in the nucleus of this cell. Only its form changes.

text.en: The cell makes none until it is about to divide, and it is lost again after the division.

feedback.en: The DNA is present all the time. It is not made only for division.

text.en: It has been stored away inside the nucleolus, which holds all of it between two divisions.

feedback.en: The nucleolus is where ribosomal subunits are made. DNA is in the chromatin.

explanation.en: In a non-dividing cell, DNA is present as part of thread-like chromatin material. When the cell is about to divide, the chromatin material gets organised into rod-shaped chromosomes.

hints.en: Are chromatin and chromosomes different materials?
